title: SurfaceFlinger, Hardware Composer, and End-to-End Frame Tracing

scout.purpose: Understand surfaceflinger, hardware composer, and end-to-end frame tracing as a causal Android engineering system rather than a vocabulary item.
scout.realWorldUse: Expert Android diagnosis requires tracing responsibility through processes, framework services, threads, queues, graphics buffers, and system composition.
scout.outcome: You can explain, inspect, test, and safely apply surfaceflinger, hardware composer, and end-to-end frame tracing.

blocks.text: SurfaceFlinger owns display composition. Around display refresh it examines visible layers, latches eligible new buffers, applies SurfaceControl metadata, and asks Hardware Composer how layers should be composed. Device composition can use display hardware planes; client composition uses GPU work into an output buffer before HWC presents it. WindowManager supplies window and layer policy metadata but does not render app pixels. If no new buffer is ready, SurfaceFlinger may reuse the previous one.

blocks.text: Layer count, transforms, alpha, clipping, color, protected content, overlays, and hardware capabilities influence composition choice. A SurfaceView can provide a separate layer composed by SurfaceFlinger, while TextureView content is generally integrated into the app UI layer. Extra layers may enable efficient video or independent updates but add synchronization and policy complexity. Presentation fences indicate completion at later pipeline points. A late buffer can miss latch even if its producer finished close to the boundary.

blocks.text: Build one Perfetto frame map from input through app main work, RenderThread, GPU, BufferQueue, SurfaceFlinger latch, HWC decision, and presentation. Correlate actual and expected frame timelines and use dumpsys SurfaceFlinger or Winscope only as supporting snapshots. Compare a jank caused by app production with one caused by composition. Test overlays, video, transitions, rotation, multi-window, and refresh changes. Report uncertainty when vendor GPU or HWC detail is unavailable rather than assigning every gap to the app.

Platform internals are a causal map for diagnosis, not an invitation to depend on hidden APIs. Trace ownership across process, thread, Binder, token, queue, buffer, and display boundaries; distinguish public contracts from release-specific implementation. Use AOSP source matching the device branch, Perfetto, dumpsys, logcat, bug reports, and controlled experiments as complementary evidence. Record Android build, device, configuration, process state, workload, and timestamps. Test death, cancellation, reentrancy, backpressure, configuration, multi-window, and resource pressure. When a private class or trace label changes, the explanation should still stand at the responsibility level. Production apps use supported APIs, while platform changes require compatibility tests, security policy, boot and performance evidence, and safe rollback.

blocks.title: Common systems trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Blaming every missed frame on slow Compose or Views ignores RenderThread, GPU, buffer latch, SurfaceFlinger, HWC, and display stages.

trap_check.mistake: Blaming every missed frame on slow Compose or Views ignores RenderThread, GPU, buffer latch, SurfaceFlinger, HWC, and display stages.
trap_check.why: It collapses distinct ownership or timing boundaries and can produce a confident but incorrect diagnosis.
trap_check.fix: Trace the complete causal path with matching source and runtime evidence before changing the system.

trap_check.mistake: Depending on a hidden API, internal class name, trace label, or one device observation as a stable application contract.
trap_check.why: Platform implementation and vendor behavior can change while public compatibility guarantees remain different.
trap_check.fix: Use internals for explanation and diagnosis, but implement app behavior through supported APIs and test across versions.

challenge_intro.task: Produce an end-to-end annotated frame trace for UI plus video, identify layer and composition choices, and distinguish app-production jank from system-composition delay.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The result includes a correct causal model, reproducible evidence, adverse-path testing, compatibility boundaries, and an owned regression or recovery plan.

recall.prompt: How do SurfaceFlinger and Hardware Composer divide composition?
recall.answer: SurfaceFlinger selects layers and may perform client GPU composition; HWC chooses and executes supported display composition and presentation work.

recall.prompt: What must be recorded with systems evidence?
recall.answer: The Android and app build, device, configuration, starting state, workload, process or thread context, and exact capture method.

recall.prompt: How should application code use platform-internals knowledge?
recall.answer: Use it to diagnose and reason about public behavior, not to depend on hidden implementation APIs or names.

objectives: Explain the complete ownership and timing model behind SurfaceFlinger, Hardware Composer, and End-to-End Frame Tracing.
Collect version-matched evidence that distinguishes cause from correlation.
Test adverse paths and preserve a compatible regression and recovery plan.
